chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, said:
Abu Abdillah said: Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) judged that the wergild (blood money) is inherited by the heirs, except for the brothers and sisters from the mother.
ai.seo_question: Who is excluded from inheriting blood money according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distribution of blood money (diyah) by excluding maternal siblings, a ruling derived from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) based on the precedent set by Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (AS). This exclusion highlights the distinct legal status of maternal kin in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing them from full or paternal siblings who typically share in the inheritance of the deceased's estate and compensation. The narration underscores the precision of Imami fiqh in differentiating between types of heirs when allocating financial compensations for homicide.

en.hubeali: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged that the wergild, the inheritors would inherit it except for the brothers and the sisters from the mother’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ibn Mahbub has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that Amir al-Mu’minin issued a judgment that said, ’
All heirs inherit from the wergild except brothers and sisters from the mother’s side.’”
